lots.what_it_is: Hand-knotted Persian village runner, about 285 x 112 cm, wool pile, three stepped hexagonal medallions on a charcoal pole, madder field with hooked blue guls, birds and small animal figures, ivory rosette main border. Sold as Hashtrood/Azari. The design is also consistent with Hamadan-district village weaving, so the attribution is plausible but not certain. No labels or marks.
lots.score_reason: A decent-looking village runner in good pile. Persian runners of this size at Australian general auctions usually make low to mid hundreds. No verified sold comp, and the surviving prices are dealer asking prices and a passed-in lot for different rugs.
